newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial shares power to new high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial shares power to new high.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares powered ahead on Friday as investors deserted the local money market where interest rates are forecast to slip on the back of a sharp fall in annual inflation to 13.9 percent in November from 20.2 percent in October, brokers said.
The key 57-stock industrial index surged 124.84 points, or 1.5 percent, to a new all time high of 8,334.55 -- a leap of 277.29 points on the week.
"The market is going only one way and that's up. People are excited about the November inflation figure and leaving the money market where rates are goind down," one broker said.
"The rain that's falling is also helping a lot and if it continues the market will surge," he added.

Leading Friday's winners on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange, horticultural firm Ariston soared 800 cents to 2,600, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans jumped 200 cents to 4,000, clothing and furniture retailer Tedco surged 150 cents to 950.

Blue-chip beverages and hotel conglomerate Delta and hotel and supermarket chain Meikles each rose 100 cents to 3,600 and 2,200 respectively while soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes at 1,350 and electronics concern Apex at 150 both gained 50 cents.

Clothing retailer Truworths climbed 35 cents to 810, pork processor Colcom added 25 cents to 365, transport group Clan put on 20 cents to 370 and tyre re-processor and rubber products-maker NTS traded 15 cents up at 405.

Against the trend, glass firm PG dropped 10 cents to 450 on the back of its half-year results which showed lower profits and interim dividend. Sugar-cane grower Hippo also bucked the trend, shedding 10 cents to 950.

Minings continued subdued with nickel producer Bindura and Falgold trading unchanged while gold miner Rio Tinto rose 100 cents to 3,100. The seven-share mining index put on 7.55 points to 1,073.31 -- a slide of 96.58 points on the week.
